svg.title: Test 7 mechanics — set-based iteration and fourteen substring checks
svg.desc: Visualization of test 7's mechanical structure showing first the expected_tickers set defined with curly brace syntax and comments organizing the fourteen tickers by asset class, then the loop iterating in non-deterministic order over the set elements building a search literal with the f-string template f-quote-brace-ticker-brace-quote, and finally a compact two-column grid showing all fourteen tickers with their resulting search literals each marked with a green check indicating found in source.
svg.text: Test 7 mechanics — set iteration, f-string literal, fourteen substring checks
expected_tickers is a SET (curly braces, no key/value pairs):
For each ticker_symbol in expected_tickers, build a search literal with this f-string:
All fourteen iterations succeed — each quoted ticker is found in NB01's source:
Sets have no iteration order in Python — CPython uses hash-based ordering, so the loop may visit "DBC" first or "SPY" first.
That non-determinism does not affect the test: every element must pass, regardless of the order it is visited.
The search literal is just `f'"{ticker}"'` — a quoted ticker — because NB01's TICKERS is a list of strings,
not a dict. The double quotes around the ticker are what disambiguate it from incidental mentions in comments.
14 / 14 assertions pass → test green → the locked universe is intact.
